question: Should exec denylist policy remain unioned across openclaw.json and the host-local exec-approvals.json, including the documented node-local hard-denial case, or should one persisted surface become canonical?
rationale: Both choices are implementable, but they define permanent operator expectations and cross-host security semantics that cannot be selected safely from code quality alone.

options.title: Keep dual stricter-wins policy
options.body: Retain both layers, document which machine owns each layer and the node-local prompt limitation, and require exact-head native proof before merge.

options.title: Use host approvals only
options.body: Remove tools.exec.denylist and make exec-approvals.json the sole persisted denylist owner to avoid competing policy surfaces.

options.title: Pause the feature
options.body: Defer landing until the distributed-host ownership and native proof requirements can be resolved without ambiguity.

recommendation.title: Keep dual stricter-wins policy
recommendation.body: Retain both layers, document which machine owns each layer and the node-local prompt limitation, and require exact-head native proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent exec-policy history and this PR's discussion route the persistent security-policy decision to steipete.
